segments.source: Two measurements are uncertain intervals. A is between 10 and 14. B is between 13 and 17. A statement “A is definitely greater than B” is valid only if A’s minimum is greater than B’s maximum.
For a definite comparison under interval uncertainty, test the worst cases. Overlapping intervals usually prevent a strict guaranteed ordering.
Can we conclude that A is definitely greater than B? What comparison is justified?
1. A minimum=10, maximum=14; B minimum=13, maximum=17. 2. Test A_min > B_max: 10>17 is False. 3. If false, at least one allowed pair of values defeats the “definitely greater” claim.
No. The intervals do not justify saying A is definitely greater than B.
Robust conclusions must remain true across all values allowed by the uncertainty.

Problem 706. Counterfactual intervention: close the gate
Counterfactual reasoning asks what the model predicts if one condition were changed while the rest of the causal structure is held fixed.

Causal rules for a simplified town model: heavy rain → high river; high river AND unclosed gate → flooded square; flooded square → market closes. Actual facts: heavy rain occurred and the gate was not closed. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 12 members, requires at least 7 present for quorum, and 11 are present.

A counterfactual intervention changes one specified fact and then recomputes consequences from the rules. Keep all other stated rules the same unless the intervention changes them. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Under the intervention “close the gate”, what changes in the consequences? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?

1. Actual chain gives high river, then flood, then market closure. 2. Intervene: set gate=closed. 3. The flood rule requires an unclosed gate, so flooding no longer follows. 4. Without flooding, market closure does not follow. Cross-domain check: compare 11 with 7; 11≥7 is true.
With the gate closed, the model no longer implies flooding or market closure. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
